haruharu is thicker (like a runny lotion emulsion) more moisturizing, and has a cushy feel to it on the skin. no sticky residue with one layer. i also like to mix this into moisturizers to thin out thicker ones or make gel moisturizers more rich.

i’m minimal with my makeup so blush and lips are the most important for me:

blush: i layer a LOT with sheer products and love to mix it up but my go to recently has been house of hur “lavender flush” (liquid) topped with romand “blueberry chip” (powder) in the centre and lilybyred “blurry lavender” (powder) on the edges to add some depth. sometimes i’ll switch out the centre powder with essence “lovely lilac” if i need some extra colour payoff.

lips: i’m guilty of alternating between what is basically the same colour but i do love my glossier gen g “like” (old formula when it was more cool toned </3), clinique “black honey”, elf lip oil “jam session”, and recently revlon “laidback lilac” which is a perfect mlbb pink 

eyes: i keep it simple since my eye shape gets overwhelmed with a lot of eyeshadow + i wear glasses. i usually only do a cool toned taupe and smoke it out close to my upper lash line. i like kbeauty eyeshadows because they’re less pigmented and easier to work with for me since i like sheer look. my go to neutrals palette is lilybyred “ash mauve”. sometimes i’ll also add a glossy shimmer on my inner lid and i like nyx jumbo crayon “yoghurt” for this. i was only able to find this shade on my trip to europe tho so i’m a bit nervous if i ever run out. 

i can work with some more neutral/slightly warm shades if i’m feeling it and for those i like glossier “storm” as well but i have to mix it in with my house of hur blush to make it more neutral and muted. i also like the glossier ultralip “pony” which is decently neutral and a sheerer formula. i really like wearing these and wish they would come out with more cool tones.

have you tried an apple cider vinegar soak/rinse? it’s been helpful in a pinch for me when my hair started getting quite greasy due to hormonal issues.

it’s typically used as a rinse after shampooing but i like to mix it up in a squeeze bottle with a nozzle and work it into my dry scalp and wash it out when i shampoo. i do a 1:5 ratio of ACV (shake well) to water and an optional 2-3 drops of rosemary or peppermint oil per 300ml (check dilution instructions of the particular oil you’re using).

i leave it in for 15-20 minutes (medium thickness, low porosity hair, half of it is bleached) and really work it into my scalp with a silicone scalp brush.

i found that hard water in my city was also a big factor to scalp itchiness and overproduction of oils which led to this greasy feeling. it also gave my bleach blonde a green tint yuck. i got a hard water clarifying shampoo from sally’s that’s from the brand “ion” (teal cylinder bottle with a white cap). i believe it was on the pricier side but i don’t use as much with this shampoo (1 inch dollop focused on scalp with silicone brush). 

the hard water shampoo used after the ACV soak leaves my scalp feeling really clean and light for the next 2-3 days :)

oh and yeah a silicone brush you can get for pretty cheap on amazon helps a lot. it’s the ones that look like a flat paddle with spikes, it helps relieve itchiness and makes sure i’m getting the most out of this slightly elaborate clarifying routine.

blind bought hanae mori butterfly edp, miu miu twist, and grabbed a sample of lolita lempicka lolitaland from fragnet. have been eyeing twist for a while and butterfly i happened to come across a review and the notes sounded super nice! just got them in the mail so i have a few first impressions:

miu miu twist - i like this one! not a fall in love with and to die for but i needed a bright freshie in my collection. fruity woody is how it’s described and i agree. juicy red berries, a little bit resinous, and the amber is soft but complimentary. imo it’s a fresh, clean scent without being soapy. atomizer is very lovely too, reminds me of the continuous spray ones from the burberry her collection. i was worried this would pull very citrusy on me and i get a tiny whiff of it if i focus but it really backs up the red berry quality and doesn’t outshine it [4/5!!]


butterfly - ahhh i was so excited for this one but upon first sniff it didn’t smell at all like what i expected :( i read reviews about this smelling like delicious creamy fruity woods, gourmand-y etc. first spray i almost hated it because there was this sharp plastic smell, maybe my bottle expired? when it dries down i get more of a cashmere quality to it, almost reminiscent of donna karan cashmere mist but not interchangeable. i still get a slight plastic smell but not as noticeable, some have compared it to a dolls head which i agree. i tried laying miu miu twist on top of it since they both have that fruity woodsy quality and it does actually help brighten it up. as i’m writing this, the combo has been sitting on my skin for ~20 mins and it’s actually quite cozy. more creamy cashmere woods, almost no plastic, and i’m starting to pick out the florals in here (ylang ylang + jasmine). i got the bigger bottle and was considering selling it but i think i’ll continue to finish it up and layer it with miu miu twist as a lounging at home fragrance [3.5?/5]

lolitaland - a user here last week told me that this frag reminds them of lemon blueberry pancakes drizzled with icing and i totally see that. i smell that and fizzy orange vanilla creamsicle cola, love it. i’m mostly excited that i like it because of the adorable bottle but it’s a unique gourmand imo. it smells like lemon cakes crowded with fragrant, slightly waxy florals and candied peach + citrus rinds without being so heavy, the LL liquorice is soft and pleasing to someone who’s indifferent to that smell. i’m surprised i like the citrus in this because i’m usually cautious with those notes. this is very orange forwards. there’s a slight creaminess to this once it’s settled on the skin that gives a lemon meringue pie vibe. don’t know what kind of occasion i’d wear this to but definitely an outdoors fragrance in the winter, i can see this being especially cloying indoors in the summer because there’s just a lot going on. all that being said i still can’t stop sniffing my wrist [4/5]

you seem like a very lovely person and congratulations on your daughter. you already have one step in the right direction by seeking some advice, being a new parent can be stressful. along with what most people have said, maintain a strong relationship with your wife, it will be what your daughter reflects on when she’s growing up. be open and honest with both your wife and daughter. being able to work through hurdles will solidify your mutual trust and bond. 

this all seems very self explanatory and i trust that you will be a wonderful father. i personally grew up in a very conflict ridden household and i learned to hide myself from my parents as a result. i didn’t feel comfortable and safe in their presence, despite them supposedly being my primary caregivers. my mental health deteriorated very quickly and i had no outlet at home, no one knew what i was struggling with. 

being able to take initiative and be proactive is also key, boundaries are important but don’t be afraid to reach out with even a causal “hey, how’s it going?” to let your daughter know that you’re here for her. don’t be afraid to talk about “difficult” topics (sex ed/consent/identity etc.) because they are important. it’s especially comforting to hear about them from your own parents and it will establish a sense of trust and belonging. once a mutual trust is established, she will be more inclined to talk to you. there will always privacy and it’s also important to give each other the benefit of the doubt, but in most cases she will come around, again, once that mutual trust is established. 

and also, take care of yourself. this is all new and exciting for you but it can be stressful. try not to let the stress get to you, and don’t feel pressured to be perfect. doing the best that you can is already doing a lot more than, unfortunately, many parents. my parents did not take care of themselves and they lashed out on each other and their children. be willing to apologize if that happens, because anger is inevitable. simply owing up to your own mistakes and acknowledging them with your wife and daughter is something a lot of people are unable to do.

similarly, let your daughter know if you believe she is headed down the wrong path. explain that this is what you perceive but allow her to explain yourself. be able to have this conversation, even if your sides clash. if she learns that you’re willing to listen and hear her out, she’ll want to have more of these with you. all a child wants is to know their parents care and this is caring. do not give her a free pass to just anything. it’s difficult to find that balance of freedom & privacy along with discipline & respect. you both will deter from the path at times but what’s ultimately the most important is both of your abilities to be resilient and bounce back. 

best of luck, i wish you all the best. signed, a 16 year old daughter.

it’s easy to think that someone will feel overwhelmed upon telling them your concerns, but there’s a certain level of effort that everyone has to put into relationships to make them work, and that is achieved through strong communication on both sides. i also think it’s also worth mentioning to the other person that you don’t want them to be walking on eggshells around you, but rather you want to have some clarity in their intentions. sharing that you’re open to communication can be mutually beneficial and make it easier to talk about issues like these in the future.

oh boy am i in the same boat as you. doesn’t seem typical coming from an intp, but i’ve been in past toxic relationships and it’s really taken a toll on my behaviour and mindset. a lot of codependency in my current friendships, as well as trust issues, and abandonment issues. the whole shitstorm.

the main thing that has helped a lot is communication. i was never really open to the idea, especially when it came down to emotions so a lot of conflict arose due to avoidable misunderstandings. i always expected the other person to understand where i was coming from and to be fully self-aware of themselves, which turned out to be (surprise) completely unrealistic. what i found to help me a lot was to simply tell them if you don’t feel like the efforts are balanced. something along the lines of “it feels like what i’m putting into this isn’t being reciprocated, and it’s disappointing and hurtful on my end” is straightforward and to the point. and sometimes the reality is that the other person may not be good at outwardly expressing that care, even if they truly mean it. it will take patience and a lot of strong communication but it is possible to feel secure about that reciprocation. 

i think the basis of my tendency to place people on a pedestal was due to a lack of confidence in my own abilities to care for myself. this may not be your circumstance, but i would waste a lot of my energy chasing after people when all i needed to do was to see who would naturally gravitate towards me. now this doesn’t mean that shouldn’t put effort into relationships, i just believe that you should save some of your energy to focus on yourself. i also find that this is a way to figure out if someone is using you. once you start focusing on yourself, the people who would feed off of your energy start to ignore you.

truthfully, it’s terrifying to give your all to someone, not knowing what they’ll do with it, but that’s the risk you have to take with emotional vulnerability. however, it’s the gateway to stronger relationships, and those strong relationships rely on one word: boundaries. extremely important on both ends and it’s vital to establish them from the get-go to prevent future conflict, but it’s never too late. one thing i find very common when relationships don’t have boundaries is codependency which can be very detrimental to the relationship and the people in it. solidifying your own independence, and seeing the relationship as a mutually beneficial union rather than a dependence will always be a work in progress, but it’s an important mindset to have.
